about.tagline: I build applications. I integrate AI. I automate the rest.
about.summary: Full Stack developer focused on real architecture and infrastructure. I build complete applications, integrate AI, and automate processes so they work in production environments.
about.tech_1: Full Stack without friction: React on the front, Laravel or Node.js on the back, from idea to production.
about.tech_2: APIs & integrations: REST, auth with JWT/OAuth, external services, Firebase.
about.tech_3: Real infrastructure: Docker, Nginx, Linux VPS, Raspberry Pi, Synology NAS.
about.tech_4: AI in production: Gemini API, prompt engineering, rate limiting, fallbacks.
about.tech_5: Automation: n8n, no-code/low-code flows integrated into real projects.
about.story_p1: I didn't come to development by accident. I've always needed to understand how things work from the inside.
about.story_p2: I started with a Pedagogy degree, and that gave me something I still rely on today: the ability to analyze, structure, and explain complex things until they make sense. To understand systems, not just use them.
about.story_p3: But I also discovered something else: I need to create. I need to build. I need to improve what already exists. I have a natural ability to quickly spot where something breaks and what an application is missing to work better, feel clearer, or run more efficiently.
about.story_p4: Technology was always present. At 12 I was already digging through forums to fix whatever broke at home. Later, as a hobby, I set up my own servers, Raspberry Pi, Docker, automations… Not because I had to, but because I love testing new technologies, experimenting with code, and tinkering with anything that can be taken apart and rebuilt.
about.story_p5: When I started DAW I wasn't starting from zero: I was giving formal structure to something I'd been doing for years. That's when I understood that what I do isn't just programming. It's building complete systems.
about.story_p6: Today I build full stack applications knowing what happens after deploy. I configure infrastructure, automate processes, integrate AI into production, and make sure everything works even when no one is watching.
about.story_p7: I'm not interested in something that ‘looks like’ it works. I want it to actually work.
about.diff_detail: I don't ship something that doesn't work well. I look at what others overlook: edge cases, boundary conditions, the things that break when no one's watching. Not perfectionism — standard.
about.diff_selflearner: I learned before anyone taught me. Docker, Linux, AI, infrastructure — all before they appeared on any syllabus. I don't wait for someone to explain things: I research, test, break, and fix.
about.diff_pedagogy: Pedagogy gives me something pure technical training rarely does: the ability to structure, document, and make systems understandable to real people. I don't just build — I make sure what I build can be maintained and explained.
about.diff_ai: AI in production, not in demos. Gemini integrated with rate limiting, fallbacks, and error handling.
about.diff_n8n: I don't just build the app — I automate what runs behind it. n8n flows that replace repetitive work and connect systems that wouldn't talk to each other otherwise.

about.cta_desc: Available for projects where technical quality and real execution are a priority.
about.bio_p1: Technology has been part of my life for years. Even before starting my training as a developer, I was already experimenting with assembling home servers and configuring my own environments to understand how systems worked on the inside.
about.bio_p2: I am a Higher Technician in Web Application Development, where I have consolidated a solid foundation in Full Stack development, databases, web architecture, and systems integration.
about.bio_p3: Additionally, I am a graduate in Pedagogy. This background directly influences how I work: I have a structured, analytical mindset oriented towards continuous learning. I am interested in understanding processes in depth and building solutions that are clear, maintainable, and well-designed.
about.bio_p4: For years I have also worked with 3D printing. My first printers lacked connectivity, so I configured my own servers using Raspberry Pi to monitor them remotely over WAN. These types of personal projects have reinforced my ability to research, test, document, and solve technical problems autonomously.
about.bio_p5: I have completed training in cybersecurity because I believe development and security must go hand in hand. Many vulnerabilities are born in the programming phase, and as a developer, I am interested in building secure applications from the ground up. Next year I will continue expanding this specialization.
about.bio_p6: I share part of my projects and technical processes on my own channel, which has allowed me to develop documentation and technical communication skills, key abilities for working in a team and transmitting solutions clearly.
about.bio_p7: I define myself as a creative, restless, and persistent person. I like technical challenges and finishing what I start. When something blocks me, I investigate until I understand and solve it. That combination of curiosity and constancy is the engine of my professional evolution.
about.bio_p8: My goal is to continue growing within web development and systems integration, providing real value in projects where technical quality and continuous improvement are a priority.
